name: Congenital Hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Hemangioma

criteria.description: Vascular tumor fully formed and present at birth
Rapid involution within the first 12-18 months (RICH subtype) or no involution (NICH subtype)
Characteristic imaging findings on Doppler ultrasound or MRI showing high-flow vascular lesion with well-defined margins
Negative immunohistochemical staining for GLUT1 differentiates from infantile hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a fully formed vascular tumor at birth with characteristic imaging findings and either rapid involution or no involution pattern
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology and immunohistochemistry may assist in differentiation from infantile hemangioma.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fully formed vascular tumor present at birth
Rapid involution of lesion within first 12-18 months (RICH subtype)
searchTerms: rapid shrinking of vascular lesion in infancy
fast involution of birthmark in first year
vascular lesion that does not shrink
fast blood flow in vascular lesion

common.symptomName: Overlying skin discoloration (purple or red hue)
searchTerms: skin over lesion is purple or red

common.symptomName: Palpable thrill or bruit over lesion
searchTerms: vibration or sound felt over lesion

occasional.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure in large lesions
searchTerms: heart failure from large vascular lesion

rare.symptomName: Compression of adjacent structures causing functional impairment
searchTerms: pressure on nearby structures causing problems

laboratory: Normal platelet count or mild thrombocytopenia in complicated cases
Normal coagulation profile unless complicated by Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon (rare)
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing high-flow vascular channels with well-defined margins
MRI demonstrating well-circumscribed lesion with flow voids and no surrounding edema
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Negative GLUT1 immunohistochemical staining differentiates from infantile hemangioma

distinguishingFeatures: Not fully formed at birth; appears within first weeks of life
Typically undergoes proliferative phase before involution
Present at birth but grows proportionally with child
Low-flow or high-flow depending on subtype but lacks tumor characteristics

redFlags: Rapid lesion growth causing airway or vital structure compression
Ulceration with secondary infection or bleeding
references: Dubois J, et al. Congenital Hemangiomas: Clinical and Imaging Features. Radiographics. 2019.
North PE, et al. GLUT1: A Marker for Infantile Hemangiomas. Am J Pathol. 2000.
